mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility is a leading indicator of discretionary retail trips; the sustained 20.7% below-baseline reading at t-0w predicts that RETAIL_REC will remain lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days when TRANSIT has been below -15% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses below -20% from baseline, local authorities typically impose stricter stay-at-home orders, which directly suppress retail-and-recreation mobility; this predicts a further drop in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days rises relative to the prior 7 days after TRANSIT crosses below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint occurrence of elevated RESIDENTIAL (>5%) and depressed WORKPLACES (<-5%) indicates a broad shift to remote work and home confinement; this interaction reduces trip chaining to retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days when RESIDENTIAL >5 and WORKPLACES < -5.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous declines in PARKS and TRANSIT signal reduced permitted outings; because retail-and-recreation venues are subject to the same restrictions, RETAIL_REC will decline further over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: In a tightening-restrictions regime, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not lower than over the prior 14 days when PARKS < -10 and TRANSIT < -15.

mechanism_narrative: Spring seasonality normally lifts retail-and-recreation activity in late March, but this year the concurrent sharp drop in TRANSIT and PARKS indicates pandemic restrictions are overpowering seasonal tailwinds, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -4.3 to -17.3 over t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC next 28 days is higher than last 28 days despite TRANSIT and PARKS remaining below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A collapse in grocery-and-pharmacy mobility from its panic-buying peak (from +6.6% to +0.3%) signals that stockpiling has ended; reduced grocery trips spill over into fewer overall retail outings, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not lower than over the prior 7 days when GROCERY_PHARM falls below +1% after exceeding +5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL combined with a fall in PARKS indicates that people are staying home rather than engaging in outdoor recreation; this interaction reduces retail-and-recreation visits through fewer trip chains, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days when RESIDENTIAL >5 and PARKS < -5.

mechanism_narrative: Under a lockdown/pre-reopening regime, TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below -15% and -5% respectively indicate that non-essential trips are banned; this regime-conditional suppression will keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: In a lockdown/pre-reopening regime, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days when TRANSIT < -15 and WORKPLACES < -5.
